articles.title: Stage 1: Quantities, force and work

articles.summary: The Fourier series decomposes a signal into oscillations.

articles.title: Stage 2: The transmission-line equations
articles.summary: So far, lines were ideal connections.

articles.title: Stage 3: Waves under sinusoidal excitation
articles.summary: With phasors, the partial differential equations become an ordinary differential equation in position.

articles.title: Overview: Foundations 1 – Vectors and Matrices
articles.summary: Data as lists of numbers, models as linear maps

articles.title: Vectors: data as lists of numbers
articles.summary: A computer can only handle numbers.

articles.title: The dot product
articles.summary: Two vectors with the same number of components give a single number if you multiply their components pairwise and add the products.

articles.title: Norms: the size of a vector
articles.summary: How large is a vector?

articles.title: Distances and units
articles.summary: Two examples are similar if their vectors lie close together.

articles.title: Angles and similarity
articles.summary: Two vectors can point in similar directions even if they have different lengths.

articles.title: Matrices and the data matrix
articles.summary: A dataset consists of many vectors with the same number of components.

articles.title: The matrix–vector product
articles.summary: The same weighted sum is to be computed for all examples of a dataset.

articles.title: Linear maps
articles.summary: A matrix is not only a table but also a rule of calculation that turns one vector into another.

articles.title: The matrix product
articles.summary: Two linear maps applied one after the other again give a linear map, and therefore a matrix.

articles.title: Transpose, symmetry and the Gram matrix
articles.summary: If you swap the rows and columns of a matrix, you get its transpose.

articles.title: Identity matrix and inverse
articles.summary: Some linear maps can be undone, others cannot.

articles.title: Systems of linear equations
articles.summary: So far the input x was given and the output Ax was sought.

articles.title: Independence, basis and rank
articles.summary: Some vectors in a list bring nothing new, because they can be put together from the others.

articles.title: The determinant
articles.summary: A linear map deforms the grid of the plane, and in the process areas become larger or smaller.

articles.title: Elementwise calculations and tensors
articles.summary: Not every calculation with vectors and matrices is a matrix product.

articles.title: Key points so far
articles.summary: Data as lists of numbers, models as linear maps

articles.title: Overview: Foundations 2 – Projection, Eigenvalues and Decompositions
articles.summary: Nearest points, natural directions and the building blocks of a matrix

articles.title: Orthonormal bases and orthogonal matrices
articles.summary: Some coordinate systems are especially convenient: their axes are perpendicular to one another, and the unit has the same length on every axis.

articles.title: Projection onto a line
articles.summary: A point lies off a line.

articles.title: The best approximate solution
articles.summary: A system of equations with more equations than unknowns usually has no solution.

articles.title: Projection onto a subspace
articles.summary: The previous section found the closest point of a column space.

articles.title: Quadratic forms
articles.summary: After the linear functions, the quadratic ones are the simplest functions of several variables.

articles.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
articles.summary: A matrix rotates and stretches most vectors at the same time.

articles.title: Diagonalization and the spectral theorem
articles.summary: If you describe a matrix in a basis of its eigenvectors, it becomes diagonal: each coordinate is only multiplied by its eigenvalue, and coupled calculations break down into separate ones.

articles.title: Positive definite matrices
articles.summary: A quadratic form is a bowl if it is positive everywhere except at the origin.

articles.title: The singular value decomposition
articles.summary: Eigenvectors exist only for square matrices, and they are perpendicular to each other only for symmetric ones.

articles.title: Approximation by matrices of low rank
articles.summary: The singular value decomposition orders the building blocks of a matrix by their size.

articles.title: The pseudoinverse
articles.summary: In Foundations 1, only a square matrix with independent columns had an inverse.

articles.title: The condition number
articles.summary: Measured data are never exact, and a computer rounds at every step.

articles.title: Key points so far
articles.summary: Nearest points, natural directions and the building blocks of a matrix
